title: Lanin society engagements and Kennedy inaugural with Sinatra
summary: He describes Lanin's society dates in Washington, Grosse Pointe and Texas, and the Kennedy inaugural night when Sinatra recognized him.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: But let's go back to Lester. When I joined Lester, he played most of the big hotels, every known hotel in New York and then we'd take trips into Washington. We'd go play at the White House and we played at the April in Paris Ball, the Hunt Ball and

all the important functions of society people and we'd go to Grosse Point, Michigan to play for the Fords and then we'd go to Wilmington to play for the DuPont people. And it was wonderful to see all these people with a lot of bread, they'd throw bread around like there was no more tomorrow, you know. Then we'd take flying trips to Dallas to play for Mr. Hunt who is one of the billionaires in oil in Ft. Worth, Texas. He imported the band over and one time when Lester was booked for the ball in Ft. Worth Louie was there, so we got acquainted altogether again with Louie and I think Trummy Young [with him] was, at this time, and Edmund Hall. And Velma was still with him, that's the time -- and then another time during the inauguration balls of practically all the presidents, it was at the Kennedy ball that we played at the inauguration, that we played at Paul Young's restaurant across from The Mayflower in Washington so we were on a little bandstand, very small bandstand, it was about, only about five men and we were waiting for the important people to come in, President-elect Kennedy and pretty soon here they come, we didn't play any music until they arrived. And so Lester is standing in front of the bandstand, he's saluting like this while they're going by and in walked
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
President-elect Kennedy, well he was president, he was inaugurated then, so I can safely say he was president. President Kennedy, Frank Sinatra, Peter Lawford and Sammy Davis, Jr. --
Oh, yes, they called themselves The Clan.
And Dean Martin and Joey Bishop.

No Dean wasn't there. It was just those four, I think, that came in so you couldn't help -- Sinatra was looking all the way around, he looked at the band and he caught my eye. He stopped in the center of the dance floor and said, "Hey, Chief, come here." He came over to me, I couldn't leave the bandstand because the other guys were in front of me, so he walked over here, he almost knocked over the saxophone players to get to me. He remember me when we were in Italy when I was on a tour with him and he remembered. I was so knocked out when he came to recognize me. He didn't say anything to anybody, not even to --
Oh, it was wonderful to play there. That's some of my experiences with Mr. Lanin and all the important personages.
